Coming on to findings on headline measures of satisfaction, Table 4.38 shows the results in relation to overall satisfaction with the bus services in question.  The overall figures for Greater Manchester, from the Bus Passenger Survey for 2018, is an 87% level of satisfaction.
rows: Table 4.38: Overall, taking everything into account, how satisfied are you with your bus journey?
Of which: Very or Fairly Satisfied

rows: Table 4.39:  Are you likely to recommend this bus service to a friend or relative?

caption: Further detail on some key aspects of satisfaction with service provision is provided in the following five tables.  The first of these homes in on bus stop provision (Table 4.40).
rows: Table 4.40:  Thinking of the bus stop you used today, how satisfied or dissatisfied were you?

caption: In terms of service frequency, Table 4.41 sets out levels of satisfaction with the different services.  The figures for the Vantage services, at 85% satisfaction, demonstrate a 24 percentage points increase on the baseline figure of 61% for the X34/32 services
rows: Table 4.41:  Thinking generally about this bus route, how satisfied are you with the following?  The frequency of services on the route

caption: Table 4.42 shows a high proportion of V1/V2 users who are “Very satisfied” with levels of reliability on the Vantage services (48%) with 82% either very or fairly satisfied.  This compares to 65% from the baseline X34/32 services, i.e. an uplift of 17 percentage points.
rows: Table 4.42:  The reliability of services on the route

caption: Vantage services are more protected than typical bus services in Greater Manchester from traffic congestion, and this is echoed in the findings reported in Table 4.43 – with only 49% satisfied with the levels of traffic congestion in the January 2014 surveys rising to 63% in the March 2019 V1/V2 surveys.
rows: Table 4.43:  The levels of traffic congestion along the route

caption: Finally, in this section, results on satisfaction in relation to the ability to change to other forms of transport are set out (Table 4.44).  For the V1/V2 this stands at 68%, up from 50% from the surveys on the X34/32 services.  These figures reflect the greater range of opportunities to connect at different points within and across the city centre brought about by bus services that traverse the city centre.
